import numpy as np, os,re
def load():
    d=os.path.normpath(os.environ['RLM_SESSION_DIR'])
    t=open(d+'/../../sessions/'+os.path.basename(d)+'.jsonl').read().replace('\\n','\n'); G={}
    for m in re.finditer(r'(Demo pair \d+ (?:input|output)|Test input) \((\d+)x(\d+)\):\n',t):
        k,h,w=m[1],int(m[2]),int(m[3])
        rows=[r.split() for r in t[m.end():].split('\n')[:h]]
        if k not in G and all(len(r)==w and all(x.isdigit() for x in r) for r in rows):
            G[k]=[[int(x) for x in r] for r in rows]
    return G
G=load()

import numpy as np, os,re, json
from collections import deque, Counter
def load():
    d=os.path.normpath(os.environ['RLM_SESSION_DIR'])
    t=open(d+'/../../sessions/'+os.path.basename(d)+'.jsonl').read().replace('\\n','\n'); G={}
    for m in re.finditer(r'(Demo pair \d+ (?:input|output)|Test input) \((\d+)x(\d+)\):\n',t):
        k,h,w=m[1],int(m[2]),int(m[3])
        rows=[r.split() for r in t[m.end():].split('\n')[:h]]
        if k not in G and all(len(r)==w and all(x.isdigit() for x in r) for r in rows):
            G[k]=[[int(x) for x in r] for r in rows]
    return G
G=load()
for p in (1,2):
    I=np.array(G[f'Demo pair {p} input']); O=np.array(G[f'Demo pair {p} output'])
    ch=[(i,j) for i in range(20) for j in range(20) if I[i,j]==3 and O[i,j]==1]
    u=[(i,j) for i in range(20) for j in range(20) if I[i,j]==3 and O[i,j]==3]
    dirs=[(di,dj) for di in (-1,0,1) for dj in (-1,0,1) if (di,dj)!=(0,0)]
    # features: multiset of neighbor values (0,2,3?)
    def feats(cells):
        out=[]
        for i,j in cells:
            nb=[I[i+di,j+dj] if 0<=i+di<20 and 0<=j+dj<20 else -99 for di,dj in dirs]
            nz=sum(1 for v in nb if v==0); n2=sum(1 for v in nb if v==2)
            out.append((nz,n2,Counter(nb).most_common(1)[0][1]))
        return out
    print('pair',p,'CHANGED feat ranges nz:',Counter(x[0] for x in feats(ch)))
    print('           unchanged nz:',Counter(x[0] for x in feats(u)))
    print('           CHANGED n2:',Counter(x[1] for x in feats(ch)))
    print('           unchanged n2:',Counter(x[1] for x in feats(u)))

steps.text:
Let me look at the stamps visually: flipped iso-2s have full 3x3 F rings (FFF/FIF/FFF), stayed ones are isolated with no surrounding 3s. So rule isn't per-cell — it's about which iso-2 gets a stamp. What distinguishes (5,14) flip from (8,16) stay? The stamp cells: maybe rule = flip iff there EXISTS an adjacent orthogonally... no, both same pattern.

Key difference: (5,14) has 3s ALL around; (8,16) has none. Maybe the actual global rule: 3-cells flip to 1 iff they touch a 2 that is NOT part of a "line" or not aligned with another 2? Alternatively: 2s lie on lines through the 3-block; stamps appear around 2s that are inside/near the main 3 region. Actually all stamped iso-2s are adjacent to large 3-blocks, unstamped ones aren't (in 3x3 window). But cells far away also stay.

Maybe rule: a 3-cell flips iff it is within Chebyshev distance 1 of an iso-2 AND ... hmm but (8,16) iso2 has no 3 neighbors, so no cell flips near it, consistent! And flipped stamps are exactly 3x3 blocks of 1s around iso-2s. Unstamped iso-2s have no 3 neighbors in their neighborhood. import itertools
def feat_table(p):
    I=np.array(G[f'Demo pair {p} input']); O=np.array(G[f'Demo pair {p} output'])
    H,W=I.shape; iso2={next(iter(cc)) for cc in comps(I,2) if len(cc)==1}
    rows=[]
    for i in range(H):
        for j in range(W):
            if I[i,j]!=3: continue
            # features
            niso=sum((i+di,j+dj) in iso2 for di,dj in dirs8)
            def vis(didx):
                ni,nj=i+didx[0],j+didx[1]
                while 0<=ni<H and 0<=nj<W and I[ni][nj]!=2:
                    ni+=didx[0]; nj+=didx[1]
                return 0<=ni<H and 0<=nj<W and (ni,nj) in iso2
            nv=sum(vis((di,dj)) for di,dj in dirs8)
            # does ANY 2 exist in that direction anywhere?
            def sees_any(didx):
                ni,nj=i+didx[0],j+didx[1]
                while 0<=ni<H and 0<=nj<W and I[ni][nj]==3:
                    ni+=didx[0]; nj+=didx[1]
                return 0<=ni<H and 0<=nj<W and I[ni][nj]==2
            nasum=sum(sees_any((di,dj)) for di,dj in dirs8)
            # nearest 2 distance in each dir
            feats=dict(niso=niso,nv=nv,nasum=nasum,
                       y=min((abs(i-q) for q,r in iso2),default=99),
                       x=min((abs(j-r) for q,r in iso2),default=99),
                       cheb=min(max(abs(i-q),abs(j-r)) for q,r in iso2),
                       diag=max(-99,-99))
            rows.append((feats,int(O[i,j])==1,i,j))
    return rows
# For each pair compute stats
for p in (1,2,3):

    tab=collections.defaultdict(lambda:[0,0])
